subsections.title: Cryptocurrency volatility modelling
subsections.primary_claim: GARCH-family models adequately capture Bitcoin volatility with heavy-tailed innovations; Paper 10 takes realized Bitcoin volatility as given and examines cross-market information content.
subsections.positioning: Paper 10 does not propose a new volatility model; complements the vol-modelling literature with cross-market identification.

subsections.title: Fear-channel mechanisms and implied volatility
subsections.primary_claim: VIX is a canonical forward-looking equity fear gauge; retail-dominated crypto markets may transmit negative-tail sentiment into institutional equity fear.
subsections.positioning: Motivates directional-asymmetric spillover from BTC downside to VIX as empirical signature of retail-to-institutional fear channel.

subsections.title: VIX-crypto and cross-market volatility spillover
subsections.primary_claim: Prior spillover literature uses unconditional or rolling spillover without distinguishing upside from downside branches; most studies stop at or before 2020.
subsections.positioning: Paper 10 (i) extends sample through 2026-04, (ii) integrates net-direction spillover with asymmetric Granger and tail QR, (iii) reports honest OOS DM null.

subsections.title: Asymmetric causality, quantile dependence, and regime-switching
subsections.primary_claim: Asymmetric-Granger (Hatemi-J), quantile regression (Koenker-Bassett), and regime-switching (Hamilton, Catania) are complementary identification tools; companion negative-result paper (K1214) and Paper 10 are complementary.
subsections.positioning: Paper 10 positive cross-market identification result vs K1214 companion negative single-asset BTC forecasting result; both reinforce Harvey (2016) in-sample vs OOS discipline.
